business_scope.primary_industry_name: Airport Bonded In-Flight Meal Production and Direct Ramp Delivery

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romanistic tradition with significant Anglo-American influence in commercial, corporate, and aviation matters)

Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements with Luxembourg, Netherlands, Singapore, France, Mexico, Portugal, Spain, South Korea, UAE, Qatar, Italy, and Belgium

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (as amended): national AML/CFT framework establishing CDD/EDD, PEP rules, record-keeping, and reporting obligations. UBO regime: Decreto Ejecutivo No. 129 de 4 de noviembre de 2020 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales), administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), requiring annual electronic declaration of ultimate beneficial owners. Corporate law: Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (Sociedades Anónimas), as amended. Fiscal: Código Fiscal (annual Tasa Única USD 300). Supervisory guidance: Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and Superintendencia de Bancos risk-management regulations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (accessible to DGI, UAF, Public Registry, and foreign authorities under international exchange-of-information agreements; not publicly searchable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if originating State is not a Hague Convention party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified copy of corporate Resolution and Power of Attorney (Poder) appointing the Panama incorporation attorney and resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague States)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter with AML/KYC provenance for each corporate shareholder and material UBO

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered auditor of the shareholder entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening of all UBOs, incorporators, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) Panama UAF national advisory and regulatory risk lists; and (v) UK OFSI and other material domestic lists. PEP classification follows Ley 23 de 2015 and includes domestic and foreign PEPs; identified PEPs trigger enhanced due diligence (EDD), senior-management approval, source-of-wealth review, and transaction monitoring. Adverse-media checks and aviation-security eligibility vetting are mandatory for ISIC 5621 catering operators under the Low_Risk_Standard classification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Portal de Servicios en Línea del Registro Público de Panamá - 'Reserva de Nombre / Vista' module (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name may be a distinctive designation composed of Latin-script letters, Arabic numerals, and spaces; accented Latin characters are accepted, while non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must not be identical, phonetically equivalent, or confusingly similar to any existing company, commercial name, or registered trademark in Panama, and must be followed by 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.' Official registry filings are processed in Spanish; foreign-language supporting documents require certified Spanish translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: VALORES / SECURITIES / BOLSA / STOCK EXCHANGE (prior authorization of the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores)
GOBIERNO / GOVERNMENT / PRESIDENCIA / PRESIDENCY / MINISTERIO / MINISTRY
PANAMÁ / PANAMA / REPÚBLICA / REPUBLIC (prior justification and authorization)
UNIVERSIDAD / COLEGIO / ACADEMY (prior authorization of the Ministry of Education)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation (Vista) is valid for 30 calendar days from issuance and may be renewed once for an additional 30 days if incorporation is not completed. Upon rejection, the applicant, through its resident agent, may (i) file a written recurso de reconsideración with the Director General del Registro Público within 10 business days of service, attaching legal arguments and an alternative name option; (ii) if denied, file a recurso de apelación before the hierarchical authority (Ministerio de Gobierno) within 10 business days; and (iii) ultimately pursue a contentious-administrative action before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within two months of the final administrative decision. In parallel, the applicant may file a new Vista with an alternative name to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only as the statutory registered-office address combined with a licensed resident agent (agente residente) maintaining a physical office for service of process. For the airline inflight catering production kitchen (ISIC 5621), a virtual office is NOT acceptable: the operator must evidence a physical, municipally licensed, MINSA-inspected food-production facility at the airport or off-airport bonded site, with ramp-delivery logistics and airport security access.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated 80-90%) for the catering kitchen within the first operating year, driven by MINSA food-safety inspections, municipal health checks, and Tocumen airport security audits; moderate (estimated 25-40%) for the resident-agent office during AML/CFT supervisory or registry verification exercises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927, as amended (General Corporation Law of the Republic of Panama) – Articles 1-8 (formation and contents of the Articles of Incorporation), 17 (minimum capital), 20-35 (share capital and share certificates), 36-65 (directors, officers and corporate governance), 66-72 (corporate records and registered agent duties).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Pacto Social y Estatutos (Articles of Incorporation) executed before a licensed Panamanian notary public
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum authorized capital of US$10,000.00; no statutory paid-up capital requirement exists at formation, and no escrow account mandate applies. Shares may be issued for consideration fixed by the board of directors; registry inscription fees are calculated on the authorized capital declared.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Corporation issue and allot the subscribed shares to the founding shareholders upon acceptance of consideration, and that the President and Secretary execute and deliver the corresponding share certificates; FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered office and statutory resident agent be established at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and that the resident agent be instructed to maintain legal records and accept service of process; FURTHER RESOLVED: That [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to hold office until the next annual shareholders' meeting; FURTHER RESOLVED: That the officers are jointly and severally authorized to open bank accounts, execute catering and aviation contracts, and complete all operational and sanitary licensing filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Customer Service / Online Portal (www.registropublico.gob.pa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search and reservation application (Ficha de nombre) for the proposed Sociedad Anónima, confirming that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. Pay the nominal search fee and obtain the official certificate of name reservation, which is valid for 30 days from issuance.
required_dossiers: Completed name search application form
Copy of passport or valid identification of the incorporator
Proposed corporate name with up to three alternative name options
Payment receipt for the search and reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused on grounds of similarity, file a new application using an alternative reserved name or submit a written request for reconsideration with a comparative argument before the Directorate of the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (licensed Panamanian notary public)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The resident agent drafts the Pacto Social y Estatutos in Spanish, including corporate purpose covering airport inflight catering production and direct ramp delivery. The incorporators or their designated representative appear before the notary to execute the instrument; the notary authenticates signatures and records the act in the notarial protocol. The original notarized instrument and the first protocol copy are then prepared for registry inscription.
required_dossiers: Pacto Social y Estatutos (Articles of Incorporation) in Spanish
Certificate of name reservation issued by the Public Registry
Copy of passport or valid identification of each incorporator
Registered agent acceptance letter and registered office address confirmation
Evidence of payment of notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a defect in the draft, amend the affected clause and re-execute the corrected page or execute a clarifying amendment (aclaratoria) before the same notary without restarting the entire incorporation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription with the Mercantile Section of the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Articles of Incorporation with the Mercantile Section for legal review and inscription. The Registrar examines the instrument for compliance with Law 32 of 1927, assigns a unique corporate folio, and issues the inscription certification. Upon inscription, the legal existence of the Sociedad Anónima is effective as of the execution date of the Articles.
required_dossiers: First protocol copy of the notarized Articles of Incorporation
Original certificate of name reservation
Form 3983 – official registry application and fee payment form
Proof of payment of registration fees calculated on authorized capital
Legal opinion or certification of the resident agent where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a formal observation (observación), correct the noted defects by filing a clarifying exhibit, amendment, or supplemental certificate within the statutory cure period, and request re-examination; a certified copy of the inscribed Articles is then released.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Registration Edict and Marginal Annotation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá and a national circulation newspaper accredited by the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The resident agent drafts the edict (edicto) containing the corporate name, folio, and date of inscription, submits it for Registry approval, and arranges publication once in an accredited Panama national newspaper. The published copy is then filed with the Registry, which records the marginal annotation on the registered Articles of Incorporation, thereby completing the publicity requirement.
required_dossiers: Registry-approved text of the incorporation edict
Payment receipt for publication fees
Copy of the inscribed Articles of Incorporation with folio number
Affidavit or certificate of publication issued by the newspaper
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published edict contains typographical or substantive discrepancies from the inscribed text, arrange a corrective edict publication and file a certificate of correction with the Registry to cure the inconsistency without invalidating the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Books, Registered Office Adoption, and Officer Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Resident Agent (Panama-licensed attorney) and Registro Público de Panamá (book legalization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The resident agent opens the statutory corporate books: share register, shareholders' minute book, board of directors' minute book, and share certificate stub book, and presents them for legalization where required. The registered office is formally adopted at the agent's address, the subscribers execute a written consent appointing the initial directors, and the board adopts the pro-forma First Board Resolution approving share issuance, registered office, and officer appointments.
required_dossiers: Corporate books (Registro de Acciones, Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva, Libro de Actas de la Asamblea de Accionistas)
Written consent of subscribers appointing the initial board of directors
Pro-forma First Board Resolution (as set out above)
Share certificates issued to founding shareholders
Resident agent services agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry refuses to legalize a corporate book due to formal defects, correct the pagination, notarial signature, or binding and resubmit the book; missing entries in corporate books are cured by a ratificatory shareholder resolution and a corrective board minute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Formalization: RUC, Municipal Aviso Operacional, and Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipio de Panamá (Treasury); Caja de Seguro Social (CSS); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the corporate Taxpayer Identification Number (RUC) from DGI using the registered Articles of Incorporation; apply for the Municipal Aviso Operacional covering the catering plant location; register the company as an employer with the Caja de Seguro Social; and file the workplace hygiene and safety registration with MITRADEL before commencing any operational activity.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Articles of Incorporation and corporate folio certification
Copy of the legal representative's identification and appointment certificate
Municipal Aviso Operacional application form and lease or title deed of the plant address
DGI RUC registration forms and supporting incorporation documents
CSS employer registration forms (C-1 and annexes) and MITRADEL workplace registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI, the Municipality, or CSS rejects the filing for incomplete documentation, the designated officer cures the file by submitting rectified certified documents or an explanatory letter; administrative reconsideration may be filed within five business days against an erroneous tax classification or municipal license denial.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección General de Salud (DIGESA), in coordination with Tocumen, S.A. (airport concessionaire) and the Autoridad Panameña de Seguridad de Alimentos (AUPSA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento para Planta de Alimentos (Sanitary Operating Permit for Food Plants) plus the Tocumen, S.A. Airport Operational Concession and Ramp Access Authorization (Permiso de Acceso a Plataforma)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Environmental Impact Study (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental, EsIA) applicable to industrial-scale inflight food processing plants; small semi-elaborated kitchen operations of limited capacity may qualify as Category I (Registro Ambiental) at the discretion of MiAMBIENTE.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Decreto Ejecutivo No. 18 de 1999: for discharge to municipal sewerage, pH 6.0-9.0, temperature below 40°C, BOD5 ≤ 350 mg/L, COD ≤ 600 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L, and oils and greases ≤ 50 mg/L; mandatory grease traps and oil-water separators at all cooking, washing, and scullery discharge points. Air emissions must comply with national air quality regulations including kitchen exhaust odor control, VOC and grease-particulate filtration, and proper management of refrigerated solid waste under AUPSA/MINSA protocols with licensed waste haulers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Certificado de Seguridad contra Incendios) from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, including kitchen hood and fixed fire-suppression system inspections; structural load and electrical installation certification from the Municipio de Panamá engineering division obtained through the Aviso Operacional process; workplace hygiene and safety regulations registration (Registro del Reglamento Interno de Higiene y Seguridad) with MITRADEL; mandatory Comité de Seguridad e Higiene for employers with 20 or more workers; and occupational risk (work-accident) insurance coverage registration with the Caja de Seguro Social.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official portal: Sistema Integrado de Información Tributaria (SITIO) - https://sitio.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) obtains the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) through SITIO: (1) complete incorporation at the Registro Público de Panamá and obtain the company Ficha; (2) appoint a resident agent and a local fiscal representative with power of attorney; (3) file the RUC application in SITIO declaring CIIU activity code 5621 (food service activities for transport) and estimated gross receipts; (4) attach the certificate of incorporation, corporate document amendments, and proof of Panamanian operational address; (5) receive an immediate provisional RUC and final RUC after DGI documentary validation, normally within 5-10 business days; (6) open the mandatory ITBMS tax account in the same registration process and apply for exporter status; (7) activate SITIO e-filing credentials and obtain electronic-invoicing (FEL) authorization. Non-resident ownership is expressly permitted and no paid-in minimum capital is required, although an active local operational address must be evidenced for the catering licence and DGI records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Panamanian law; the S.A. is mandatorily taxed at entity level at 25% corporate ISR on Panamanian-source income only. Available statutory elections: (1) consolidated group income-tax return for 100%-related Panamanian companies with DGI pre-approval under Código Fiscal Article 699-A; (2) micro-business simplified regime for annual gross receipts up to B/.36,000, generally unsuitable for a commercial airline catering kitchen; (3) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) and International Financial Center (IFC) licensing frameworks for qualifying exclusively offshore-source income; (4) contractual tax-stability and incentive regimes where expressly granted by law for qualifying investments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panamanian Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover exemption for ITBMS: any person commercially selling goods or rendering services in Panama must register at commencement of activities. A simplified small-taxpayer option exists for annual gross receipts up to B/.36,000; a full-scale catering kitchen exceeds that threshold and must maintain standard ITBMS registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica Panamá - FEP) governed by DGI Resolution No. 201-1579 of 2019 and implementation Resolution No. 201-2422 of 2021, phased in by annual gross-income brackets from 2021 through the final universal wave in 2023-2024. Taxpayers must issue invoices through an authorized technology provider or the DGI FEP web client and transmit each invoice in real time to SITIO; the DGI validates the transaction and returns a unique electronic authorization (FEL) number that must appear with a QR code on the invoice. Non-compliant invoices deny purchasers the input-credit entitlement and trigger seller penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the ITBMS territorial framework, the 0% export rate applies to (i) goods physically leaving Panamanian customs territory and (ii) services performed in Panama that are supplied to non-resident persons and exclusively utilised outside Panama. An airport in-flight catering kitchen may zero-rate ramp deliveries of meals and provisions to foreign-flag airlines operating international routes when title passes to the airline at the aircraft-side delivery point and the goods are consumed outside Panamanian territory. Domestic-leg supplies on Panama-to-Panama flights and sales to airport retail concessions are local supplies taxable at the standard 7% ITBMS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) filed electronically through SICE (Sistema Integrado de Comercio Electrónico) evidencing physical exit from Panamanian customs territory

Bill of Lading (Conocimiento de Embarque) or, for bonded aircraft-ramp deliveries, the signed Catering Delivery Receipt/Flight Manifest countersigned by the airline's authorized ground representative and cross-referenced to the international flight itinerary
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT/MT103 or ACH credit confirmation) showing settlement of the export invoice in the Panamanian S.A.'s local USD account
Commercial invoice annotated 'ITBMS 0% - Exportación de Alimentos a Bordo' with the corresponding airline purchase order
Aircraft and flight documentation evidencing the international route for each supplied service leg
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may reclassify zero-rated export supplies as local taxable supplies and assess 7% ITBMS with statutory moratory interest from the original due date, and may simultaneously claw back all input ITBMS credits claimed in respect of such supplies. Under the Código Fiscal as reformed by Law 70 of 2019, fraudulent export claims are penalized at 100%-300% of the omitted tax plus monetary fines, and serious cases may be prosecuted as tax crimes carrying imprisonment. False customs export declarations also attract separate aduanero penalties and retrospective reassessments. The State retains an extended limitation period to reassess and collect in cases of fraudulent export documentation. Because Panama uses the US dollar as legal tender, no statutory FX surrender rule applies; the 180-day repatriation-evidence benchmark is enforced in DGI practice as the contemporaneous substantiation standard for preserving export zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) (Panama has no issuing central bank; the US dollar is legal tender and the National Bank of Panama acts as fiscal agent for government financial services).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: No foreign exchange control regime exists. Panama operates a fully dollarized economy (balboa at 1:1 USD). Both current and capital account transactions are freely convertible; profit remittance, dividends, and loan payments face no FX approval hurdles. Only Panamanian-source income is taxable under territorial rules; dividend distributions paid by a Panama S.A. from foreign-source income are not subject to Panamanian tax.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio exists for export/airline catering receipts. All USD-denominated export proceeds may be retained in any bank account, free of surrender obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and USD Denominated Checking
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility: Panama permits foreign fintech/EMI accounts only for payment processing, not as a primary treasury settlement rail. Legal constraint: non-bank payment service providers must be licensed by SBP for local money movement; offshore digital EMIs (e.g. Wise/Revolut) generally cannot provide a Panama S.A. with a domestic Panamanian account and are not treated as regulated deposit-taking institutions for escrow requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Panamanian banks require at least one director or legal representative to appear physically for initial KYC, especially for non-resident owned S.A.; remote opening may be permitted with a Panamanian consulate notarization and apostilled corporate packet, but the bank's compliance team typically schedules a video interview, and the final risk approval is contingent on a physical visit for high-velocity aviation invoicing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance and tax avoidance red flag on non-resident S.A. bank account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Articles of incorporation and legalized corporate registry (Registro Público) copy, current good standing certificate, physical office lease or airport butchery/catering facility proof, Panamanian tax registration (RUC), board resolution designating signatories, and a business plan forecasting invoice flows with airline purchase orders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value transaction velocity in 'inflight catering' without demonstrative operational contracts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed inflight catering contracts with airlines, ISIC 5621 license from the Civil Aviation Authority (or Aerodrome Authority), HACCP food-safety certification, ramp access permit, monthly ACH/MT103 counterparty lists, and source-of-funds affidavits with bank statements of underlying customers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol: transfer USD via SWIFT (MT103) to the Panama S.A.'s USD-denominated operational account at a tier-1 Panamanian bank; the payment purpose code should be 'injection of capital' (use IMF BPM6 category 'equity investment' or OECD purpose code Z211) and include a board resolution evidencing shareholder loan or capital contribution. No exchange-control authorization is required; however, the receiving bank may request a sworn affidavit stating source of funds to meet AML regulation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: outbound USD trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for direct vendor payment, and documentary/standby letters of credit (Commercial LC under UCP600) for importing raw materials (e.g., aviation fuel and food stuffs). Local operational payments can be cleared through ACH via Banco Nacional de Panamá's Automated Clearing House for payroll and module payments; aviation contract invoices are cleared on real-time gross settlement or wire to airline treasury desks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC forward contracts in USD (no PAB/USD hedge required because 1:1 peg)
Cross-currency non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in LATAM currencies (e.g., USD/MXN, USD/COP)
Panama-based S.A. is allowed to execute currency swaps via non-resident licensed dealing rooms

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday for ISIC 5621 airline in-flight catering. The territorial regime excludes true foreign-source active income from the Panamanian tax base. Standard deductions apply for bonded raw materials, direct labour, airport concessions, refrigeration assets, and delivery vehicle depreciation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 250 (Declaración Jurada de Renta para Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically through the Panama DGI e-Tax portal of the Dirección General de Ingresos.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with mandatory monthly advance income tax payments and quarterly provisional assessments for corporations; the annual return reconciles all advances.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed no later than 31 March of the calendar year immediately following the fiscal year-end; for an approved non-calendar fiscal year, within three months after the actual fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from airport bonded catering, ramp vehicle deliveries, airline meal uplift, and ancillary kitchen services performed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned Panamanian S.A. must report only Panama-source catering revenue. Invoices billed to a foreign airline for services physically rendered and delivered inside Panama must be included; genuine foreign-source revenue, if any, is excluded with documentary evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 / Cost of Sales and Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct raw food and beverages, packaging, kitchen payroll, airport concession fees, maintenance of refrigeration/galleys, vehicle fuel, and depreciation of kitchen equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses allocable to foreign-source activities must be stripped out. Related-party transactions must be arm's length and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panamanian-source losses available for carryforward may offset future taxable profits within five consecutive years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign losses cannot be consolidated with Panama-source catering income; the loss carryforward is allowed only in the same Panamanian business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after all statutory deductions, depreciation, prior-year NOL application, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned S.A. without a permanent establishment, no local central overhead allocation is permitted unless incurred through a Panama branch or tied to Panama-source activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the headline corporate tax at 25% on Line 12 before withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are limited to Panama withholding tax certificates issued by DGI; no credit is available for foreign corporate taxes under the territorial system.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of dividends paid and the associated 10% dividend withholding tax, including advance dividend taxes paid by the corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Distributions to non-resident shareholders are final-withholding taxed at 10%; treaty relief, where a DTA exists, requires submission of the foreign tax residency certificate and beneficial ownership documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of approximately 0.5% of the final tax due, capped at 50%, plus a late-filing fine ranging from USD 50 to USD 10,000 depending on gross receipts. No daily surcharge is separately applied; Panama applies monthly recargo rules. Failure to file after official notice may result in DGI assessment, an additional 25% fraud or negligence uplift, and criminal prosecution for directors submitting false returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends distributed by a Panamanian S.A. to both resident and non-resident shareholders out of Panamanian-source taxable profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited double tax agreement network. To invoke a reduced withholding rate, the non-resident recipient must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, submit a beneficial owner declaration, and file the applicable DGI DTA relief form through the e-Tax portal before the dividend distribution date, or initiate a refund claim within the statutory limitation window if the full 10% was already withheld. The Panamanian withholding agent must retain the TRC and declaration as part of its books and records.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory withholding on payments to non-residents for industrial/commercial royalties; treaty rates commonly 5%–10% under applicable DTA. Interest: 12.5% statutory withholding on debt interest paid to non-residents; treaty rates commonly 5%–10% for arm's-length interest on commercial debt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 1,000,000 in annual related-party transactions triggers the mandatory Local File and transfer pricing affidavit; group-wide revenue above USD 10,000,000 triggers the Master File. Transactions with entities resident in tax-haven or no-tax jurisdictions can trigger documentation at a lower administrative threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations under Law 70 of 2019 apply to relevant companies and relevant activities. In-flight catering performed through a physical airport kitchen is a substantive local business: the S.A. avoids any shell-company issue by maintaining premises and kitchen equipment, employing kitchen and dispatch staff, making contracts and operational decisions in Panama, and incurring commensurate local payroll and expenditures. If instead the entity is used solely as a contractual pass-through for offshore group cuisine suppliers, the ESR failure and artificial construction doctrine will apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Income Tax Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating Panama-source airline catering revenue, suppressing cash meal uplift invoices, using fabricated supply invoices from related parties, or falsely allocating Panama-source profits to foreign-source accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil surcharge of at least 25% to 50% of the evaded tax, interest on arrears, and criminal penalties under Panamanian tax and criminal law including imprisonment from 2 to 5 years for fraudulent tax declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct false tax returns are personally and jointly liable for restitution, tax penalties, and criminal fines. Panama courts may pierce the corporate veil, impose travel bans, and order civil damages to the National Treasury.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Panama S.A. holds no catering kitchen equipment, no airport concession, no operational staff, and no inventory, but issues invoices and receives airline payments under back-to-back arrangements with offshore group entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic Substance Regulations penalties of up to USD 1,000,000, cancellation of the RUC tax identification and commercial registry, DGI deemed-profit assessments based on gross receipts, and referral for criminal fraud investigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent may be held personally liable for false substance declarations, disbarred from practicing in Panama, subjected to exit bans, and exposed to extradition requests in egregious structuring cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering Through Airport Bonded Logistics
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Co-mingling unverified cash, bearer-share concealment of the beneficial owner, or use of the inflight catering company to disguise payments connected to corrupt airline procurement, fictitious cargo permits, or unreported customs deliveries inside the bonded airport zone.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering penalties under Panamanian law carry imprisonment of 5 to 12 years, fines up to substantial statutory maxima, asset forfeiture, administrative sanctions by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF), and criminal shutdown of the catering operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, executives, and beneficial owners are individually prosecutable. Personal travel bans, passport revocation, restrictions on banking activity, and criminal confiscation apply. Nominee directors who sign AML affidavits are not shielded by the corporate form.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Related-party transactions with the airline group or offshore catering procurement affiliates exceed USD 1,000,000 and the S.A. fails to prepare and file the Local File, transfer pricing affidavit, benchmarking study, and contemporaneous arm's-length justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI transfer pricing adjustment to taxable income, a penalty of up to 25% of the adjustment, late-filing fines of up to USD 50,000, and potential loss of deductibility of the intercompany expense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify incomplete or fraudulent TP documentation may be held jointly liable for additional tax and penalties. In flagrant cases, travel restrictions and criminal sanctions for financial fraud may apply.
